description: Fewer than 4% of Palestinian applications in Area C were approved between 2015 and 2019, per the Civil Administration itself. Bimkom's data for 2016-2020: 2,550 applications, 24 approved - a rejection rate of about 99%.
energy_note: Twenty-four permits. Two and a half thousand families.

description: 282 applications submitted since October 2023, none approved, per the Israel Planning Council. The rate is no longer low; it is nil.
energy_note: Two hundred and eighty-two applications, no approvals at all.

aspect: The older baseline, for the trend
description: Over 94% of applications between January 2000 and September 2007 were denied. Palestinian construction is effectively prohibited across some 70% of Area C, and restrictions in the remaining 30% virtually eliminate the possibility of a permit.
energy_note: A quarter of a century of the same answer.

aspect: So the only option is to build without one
description: Families build anyway, because children keep being born. The house is then permanently exposed: it carries a demolition order from the day it is finished, and the order may be executed in three years or thirteen.
money_note: Cost of a house built knowing it may be demolished.
energy_note: A home with a sentence already passed on it.

aspect: Which converts a family's entire savings into a hostage
description: The house is typically the only substantial asset. Building it is not an investment; it is placing everything the family owns inside a structure the state has already declared unlawful.
energy_note: Everything you own, in a building marked for removal.

aspect: The permit refusal and the demolition are one policy
description: Refusing permits creates the illegality that the demolitions then enforce. Described separately they look like planning and law enforcement; together they are a single mechanism.
energy_note: Made illegal, then punished for it.

description: Data provided to the Israeli planning rights organisation Bimkom shows that between 2016 and 2020 Palestinians submitted 2,550 building applications in Area C and 24 were approved. Not a low rate applied to a small number - two and a half thousand families, and twenty-four permits.
